Mayor Watters congratulated the Centre Wellington Riverhawks U15 Girls Lacrosse Team on their recent achievement of winning the Division B Championship and presented them with a Certificate of Achievement.

items.title: Groves Memorial Community Hospital and Upper Grand Family Health
notes: Team System Update

Presentation from Angela Stanley, Alison Armstrong and Hilary Blackett Angela Stanley, President and CEO of Groves Memorial Community Hospital provided an update on hospital statistics, the Patient Partner Council, the Malnutrition Prevention Program for seniors, and Hospital-to- Home care initiatives. She also highlighted board governance structure, staffing updates, revenue and expenses, physician recruitment efforts, and ongoing Truth and Reconciliation initiatives.

Hilary Blackett, Executive Director of the Upper Grand Family Health Team provided a further update on the collaborative work being undertaken with Groves Memorial Community Hospital. She introduced the new Nurse Practitioner Primary Care Clinic, which is expected to launch this fall and is aiming to provide care and support for patients, newborns, and families across the community.

items.title: Monster March Parade and Township Road Closures
notes: Presentation from Sensational Elora Group (Barb Lee)

Barb Lee, a representative of Sensational Elora Group, provided an overview of the Monster March Parade and highlighted the impact of Township fees associated with the event. She noted that event proceeds are donated to the CW Foodbank and CW Eats program.
B. Lee responded to comments and questions from Council regarding costs associated with the event.
A. Gilmore responded to questions from Council regarding the fee structure and subsidies for events.

items.title: Data Centres and Future Development in Centre Wellington
notes: Presentation from Courtney Pamela

Courtney Pamela gave a presentation regarding the potential impacts that data centres may have on culture, climate, and land use, including the rapid changes associated with their development and operation.

items.title: 2026 Emergency Management Report and Presentation - Wellington
notes: County

Presentation from Linda Dickson, Emergency Manager/CEMC Linda Dickson, Emergency Manager/CEMC (Wellington County) provided the annual report, noting that the Township has completed all requirements under the Emergency Management and Civil Protection Act for 2026. She highlighted the upcoming review of the Township's Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA) and advised that no changes are proposed to the current Emergency Management Plan.
L. Dickson noted that a draft amendment under Bill 25 will be brought forward to Council after it comes into full force and effect.

items.title: Mayor's County Council Report
notes: Mayor Watters noted no major updates.

items.title: Councillor's Committee Updates
notes: Councillor Bronwynne Wilton provided an update on the Fergus BIA, noting the successful hosting of the Fergus Fibre Festival and Medieval Faire. She also highlighted the ongoing family-friendly music series Twilight at Templin Gardens held in downtown Fergus on Wednesday evenings throughout July and August.

Councillor Lisa MacDonald provided a brief update on the Victoria Senior’s Committee and noted that an announcement was made at its regular Board meeting held August 10th regarding provincial funding received for the Victoria Seniors Centre.
Councillor Jennifer Adams provided a brief update regarding the Groves Memorial Community Hospital Board, noting that the appointed board positions will be replaced with three elected positions.

Councillor Kimberely Jefferson provided an update on the Elora BIA, noting that the regular meeting was held last week. She highlighted ongoing planning efforts for Late Night Shopping and Monster Month and advised that a committee has been established to begin preparations for the 2027 budget.

items.title: Delegation on Item 12.8 re: Telecommunications Concurrence Request -
notes: 6983 Wellington Road 7, Nichol - Jessica MacCulloch, Shared Tower Inc.

Jessica MacCulloch, a representative of Shared Tower Inc., provided a delegation regarding a proposed telecommunications infrastructure project, including an overview of the company’s work in telecommunications infrastructure development, satellite internet services, and initiatives to expand wireless coverage, address service gaps, and provide high-speed internet access to rural communities across Canada.

She advised that Shared Tower is proposing the development of a 60m by 30m communications compound to support a satellite communications provider. The proposed facility would contain communications antennas approximately 2.7 m in height.

items.title: Fire Master Plan Update
notes: Report from Jason Benn, Fire Chief

Jason Benn, Fire Chief introduced the report noting that population growth, changing demographics, and increased development are expected to place greater demands on emergency response, staffing, facilities, and fire prevention services. He advised the plan identifies priorities to ensure the fire service can maintain service levels and meet future community needs.

Tim Beckett, Consultant at Behr Integrated Solutions Inc., gave a presentation on the long-term strategic plan, highlighting key findings of the Community Risk Assessment (CRA), the review and alignment of current services, evaluation of fire safety risks, assessment of core functions and operational readiness, and the development of a fiscally sustainable plan to guide future service delivery.
T. Beckett responded to comments and questions from Council regarding apparatus and community need, data collection, rescue type training, staffing and location of the relocated Fergus Station.
A. Gilmore responded to questions from Council regarding public consultation.
J. Benn responded to questions from Council regarding mutual aid agreements and associated response.

motions.item_title: Notice of Motion - Councillor Wilton - Data Centre 08-24-26
motions.text: Given the rapid growth of AI-driven systems, cloud computing and digital infrastructure has accelerated the development of new and large-scale data centres to meet industry defined needs and the fact that the Province of Ontario has not yet established a provincial regulatory framework for AI data centre industry there is cause to exercise caution regarding the introduction of data centres within the Township of Centre Wellington. 1. THEREFORE the Council of the Township of Centre Wellington directs staff to undertake a review and study costing no more than $49,999 of the Township’s land use planning policies in relation to artificial intelligence (AI) data centres, pursuant to section 38 of the Planning Act, applicable to all zones where the use is permitted in the Township of Centre Wellington, including, but not limited to, its Official Plans and Zoning By-law, and any required changes to the Township’s land use planning policies, mapping, and regulatory framework with consideration of, but not limited to the following: a. Existing Official Plan policies and Zoning By-law permissions and regulations; b. Energy use and the impacts to power grids, c. Water use and the impacts to long term drinking water quality and quantity, and d. Noise and light pollution impacts, 2. THAT staff be directed to report back to Council on the items listed above (a) in Q3 of 2027. 3. THAT staff be directed to prepare for Council’s consideration at the Council meeting on September 28, 2026, an Interim Control By- Law under Section 38 of the Planning Act, prohibiting the use of AI data centres within the study area described in (a) above.
